## Overview

Enable NVIDIA DeepSeek-V4.1 PCP decode-only CUDA graphs by stabilizing graph-read metadata and sizing decode graphs by rank-local requests. Reuses the existing MRV2 graph implementation; prefill and bounded replay remain eager. Stacked on #59857, #61553 and #61554.

## Claims

- Preserve the addresses of gathered SWA positions, compressed cache slots and compressor ring-link metadata across graph replays.
- Use the largest rank-local request count for request-sharded decode graph dispatch, while retaining global input staging.
- Allow only V4.1 `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` on CUDA; speculative graphs require the existing flattened/varlen indexer path. Unsupported configurations retain explicit guards.
- In a small, matched four-H20 experiment, short-question output throughput was **5.22× at c1 and 4.51× at c4** versus eager. This is not a long-context or general throughput claim.

## Validation

Tested parent `9516299b96954da52ce7a7416c08db2b8b9db763` versus the frozen implementation in `b2e6404` (current Python files unchanged at `34c4a21`). Four H20 GPUs, TP1/PCP4/EP4, fixed DSpark5, Humming MoE FP8 activations, dense A16, `fp8_ds_mla`, shared CPU Engram, bounded replay ON, APC OFF, chunk8192, max-seqs64, max-len131072, utilization0.85 and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` in both arms. Same read-only checkpoint mount, native runtime, packages, backend dispatch and inputs. The container's existing native extensions were reused; this was not a clean native rebuild from the candidate commit.

**Fresh sequential Graph → Eager pair**, three measured repetitions per concurrency after separate warmup. Each repetition has the same four natural GSM8K questions (prompt lengths 63/60/78/110 tokens), temperature0, thinking disabled, natural EOS and real speculative acceptance. All measured answers passed; no cache hits or length truncation. Natural output lengths vary. Throughput includes the whole request round; TPOT is first-to-last content latency divided by generated tokens minus one. Reported TPOT is the median of each round's request medians.

| Workload | Eager | Graph | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| c1 output tok/s, median [min–max] | 32.494 [31.889–32.985] | 169.756 [167.900–171.100] | 5.22× |
| c4 output tok/s, median [min–max] | 82.069 [81.581–97.824] | 369.892 [349.078–380.643] | 4.51× |
| c1 TPOT, ms | 29.293 | 5.023 | −82.85% |
| c4 TPOT, ms | 29.936 | 5.631 | −81.19% |
| c1 TTFT, ms | 143.575 | 138.941 | −3.23% |
| c4 TTFT, ms | 294.792 | 284.813 | −3.39% |
| Cold 64K/c4/output1 prefill, input tok/s | 15,255.437 | 15,265.495 | +0.066%; effectively unchanged |

Real accepted/drafted counts over the three decode repetitions:
c1 eager **1614/2385 (67.67%)**, graph **1575/2220 (70.95%)**;
c4 eager **1573/2260 (69.60%)**, graph **1618/2420 (66.86%)**.
Acceptance was neither fixed nor simulated. These results do not establish logit equivalence or unchanged acceptance on a broad corpus.

Both arms passed **32/32** fixed GSM8K canaries, with no HTTP errors or length stops. Graph additionally passed **8/8** long/ragged/replay boundary checks and **27/27** natural-EOS requests through concurrency **1→3→4→5→8→5→1**, including empty owners and changed graph shapes. Runtime target `CUDAGraph Stats` reported FULL execution (1491 counted steps across the recorded log, versus zero for eager). Draft capture completed; this alone is not evidence of draft replay.

Per-card model-load memory was **81.79 GiB** in both arms. Final graph-pool log: **0.21 GiB actual** (0.48 GiB estimated budget; an earlier profiling capture logged 0.44 GiB). Available KV budget decreased **30.79→30.31 GiB**, token capacity **8,959,121→8,818,195**. These are engine memory logs, not a sampled peak-memory comparison. No second weight layout is introduced.

<details>
<summary>All performance samples and reproduction</summary>

| Arm | C | Output tok/s, all 3 samples | Median TPOT ms, all 3 samples | Output lengths (4 requests per sample) |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| eager | 1 | 32.494, 32.985, 31.889 | 28.965, 29.293, 29.329 | 177/165/110/289; 154/165/109/208; 177/165/109/266 |
| eager | 4 | 81.581, 82.069, 97.824 | 30.651, 29.936, 28.765 | 177/160/109/255; 153/165/110/242; 179/160/110/208 |
| graph | 1 | 167.900, 171.100, 169.756 | 5.143, 5.023, 4.963 | 153/165/109/221; 177/160/109/222; 154/160/110/282 |
| graph | 4 | 380.643, 349.078, 369.892 | 5.535, 5.631, 5.902 | 159/165/110/254; 152/165/110/289; 152/160/118/270 |

Cold64K/c4 uses 8 requests per round, continuously replenished workers, output1, exact input hashes and actual cached_tokens=0. One warmup round is excluded; all three formal samples:
- Eager: 15246.559407, 15255.436697, 15261.405470 input tok/s.
- Graph: 15256.233934, 15265.495489, 15274.008424 input tok/s.

Both arms use `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`,
`VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"float8e4m3","allow_fallback":false}'`,
`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, `--moe-backend humming`, and
`--kernel-config '{"enable_jit_warmup":false}'`.
On the same launch configuration, remove `--enforce-eager` and use:
```bash
--compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[5,6,10,12,20,24,40,48],"max_cudagraph_capture_size":48}'
--cudagraph-metrics
```
The experimental ladder covers the tested DSpark5 target/draft batches through global concurrency8. It is not a universal tuning recommendation; unmatched sizes retain existing eager fallback. Both arms used the same kernel-warmup setting and graph metrics.

Raw requests, event timing, Prometheus counters, input manifests, launch arguments, startup backend audits, source hashes, failures and shutdown receipts are retained in the experiment archive. Run IDs:
- `20261014T090251Z_single_h20-56_tp1-pcp4_dspark5_replay_humming-fp8_decode-graph-full`
- `20261014T091437Z_single_h20-56_tp1-pcp4_dspark5_replay_humming-fp8_decode-graph-none`

An independent raw-data audit recomputed timings, token usage, cached tokens, answers, acceptance, input hashes and allowed source/config differences. Decode audit SHA256: `8c4adf1a8173c2e16020eaaca3d0672fbfa0e428cafa1da14d40802dcd1bd5bb`; prefill audit SHA256: `7f9a0bbd8eb6494cbd80d72543e9d11f178660792715497a71eacc233c1e05c3`. The complete raw archive is retained on the test host, not publicly attached.

</details>

**157 selected tests passed**, and all applicable pre-commit checks passed, including Ruff and mypy. Three unchanged Ray-dependent configuration cases failed in the initial wider attempt because Ray was absent; that failure log is retained. The focused rerun explicitly deselected them.

<details>
<summary>Focused test commands</summary>

From the candidate source, with its PYTHONPATH and the existing runtime:
```bash
python -m pytest --noconftest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py \
  -k 'not parallel_config_manages_decode_sharding' # 122 passed, 3 deselected
python -m pytest --noconftest -q tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py \
  -k 'zero_token_pcp_rank or v41_pcp_metadata' # 4 passed
python -m pytest --noconftest -q tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
  -k 'v41_pcp_ring_links or v41_pcp_compressor_preserves_pairs' # 14 passed
python -m pytest --noconftest -q tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py # 17 passed
```

`--noconftest` isolates these focused suites from unrelated optional dependencies. This is not a full repository test run. Existing test areas collect these worker/attention/kernel suites; the full V4.1 PCP4+DSpark FULL model configuration is not currently covered by the standard model CI, so the evidence above was collected externally.

</details>

The performance result is one sequential pair, not several independent AB/BA campaigns. These canaries are not a complete accuracy evaluation. Wider decode contexts/concurrency, repeated order reversals and broader model accuracy remain follow-ups; keep this PR Draft pending human review.

## Details

Simply relaxing the graph guard is unsafe: captured kernels retain temporary compressor/cache metadata addresses, and a global request count mismatches request-sharded decode graph dimensions. This change uses persistent metadata buffers and the existing rank-local token dispatch machinery, adding only the corresponding request count. Global staging still reserves every request. No weight, quantization, acceptance-policy, attention kernel or graph-manager implementation changes.

Incremental production diff: **5 files, +101/−8**. Review against `9516299`; the GitHub diff against main also contains the dependency stack (#59857/#61553/#61554 and the parent's MoE padding prerequisite #60946). Existing V4.1 restrictions remain: PP=DP=DCP=1, no microbatching, KV transfer, APC or MegaMoE, fixed DSpark verification when enabled. Native speculative query metadata unable to refresh empty decode owners remains rejected. Prefill graphs and prefix caching are separate work.

Credit/reuse: merged #53867 supplies generic PCP decode-only FULL graph capture/padding but retained sparse-MLA rejection. #56107 supplies replicated DSpark. #53639 concerns generic rank-local token dispatch with replicated decode. This patch supplies V4.1 metadata stability and request-sharded graph sizing; it does not claim those existing generic optimizations. ROCm #58352 handles different ragged packing. Searches found no exact duplicate of this scoped implementation.

AI assistance was used for implementation, source review and validation.

@@ -0,0 +1,104 @@
+# DeepSeek-V4.1 PCP with decoder SWA bounded replay
+
+This draft enables cold-prefill decoder trimming with PCP. It builds on
+[#59857](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59857) and
+[#61553](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61553), which supplies fixed
+DSpark verification and optional shared host Engram storage. Prefix-cache hits,
+KV transfer and CUDA Graphs for prefill remain outside this change.
+
+## Implementation
+
+Reuse the existing `ReplayBatch`, `InputBatch`, decoder replay gather kernel,
+attention builders and PCP process group. Prepare the replay builders during
+startup so their constant copies do not first run in a real request. Retain each
+existing PCP segment's intersection with the request's global scheduled tail;
+do not change token ownership or introduce another PCP partitioner.
+
+- Size per-segment replay metadata for PCP's two segments per original request.
+  Original request state remains indexed by the existing global request indices.
+- Recover each request's scheduled bounds with a CPU-group reduction indexed by
+  request state. Ignore empty segments. Stage the global tail floor separately
+  from the prefix layers' replay floor; short chunks preserve their context.
+- Agree on whether a replay batch is needed and its largest rank-local size.
+  Short or empty peers execute the same collectives with padded inputs.
+- Select the local slice of the original gathered cache slots, then gather the
+  retained slots in the same rank-major order as the new KV payload. Padding
+  carries `PAD_SLOT_ID`; it does not write cache entries.
+- Reuse the existing decoder-layer runner to gather retained rows and scatter
+  their outputs back. Zero padding is discarded rather than becoming a real row.
+- Dispatch local FlashMLA prefill/decode by token counts, since a retained batch
+  can still contain request metadata for an empty query partition.
+
+The range and padding agreements add two small host collectives per preparation;
+neither reads device tensors. Ownership remains zigzag: a single long request's
+tail can reside on one rank while peers execute padded work. This differs from
+SGLang's interleave CP layout, which distributes that tail across ranks.
+
+The model's existing guards continue to require PP=DP=DCP=1, no prefix caching,
+no KV transfer, no microbatching, and a supported MoE/attention backend. The
+NVIDIA V4.1 path supports `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` CUDA graphs while prefill and its
+bounded replay remain eager. Speculative decode requires flattened or varlen
+indexer queries; native multi-query metadata is not supported with empty PCP
+decode owners. Prefix caching remains unsupported. Fixed DSpark remains subject
+to the existing guard that its draft reads no hidden states outside the replay
+window. Requests with prompt logprobs retain all their rows.
+
+## Validation
+
+Three existing replay suites passed on H20: **27 tests**. Added coverage checks
+global-tail intersections, rank-local cache-slot selection, peer padding, empty
+query partitions and output scattering. Existing replay-start, prompt-logprobs, adaptive-boundary and graph
+regressions also pass. Unit tests mock PCP collectives; they do not by themselves
+validate a distributed model. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed.
+
+On four H20 GPUs, TP1/PCP4/EP4 with fixed DSpark5, shared Engram and
+`VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` passed 32/32 fixed GSM8K canaries (no HTTP errors or
+truncation; 3,965 of 5,645 draft tokens accepted). Eight additional checks passed:
+exact 1,023/1,025-token prompts, including full-row prompt-logprobs controls, and
+ragged concurrent 8,191/8,193/16,385/65,537-token prompts followed by natural
+decode. These use public GSM8K questions with neutral background context; they
+are targeted regressions, not a complete model accuracy evaluation.
+
+The first real trimming exposed lazy metadata-builder initialization in the hot
+path. Moving that existing initialization to startup fixed the failure while
+keeping GPU synchronization checks enabled. Failed-run evidence is retained.
+The first global-tail model also exposed a mixed batch with zero decode tokens
+but nonzero decode request metadata. Dispatching by token counts fixes the empty
+decode reshape without skipping the outer KV publication or PCP collectives.
+
+Initial cold-prefill comparison: four H20-3e GPUs, TP1/PCP4/EP4, fixed DSpark5,
+Humming A16, 8,192-token chunks, eager execution, prefix caching off. Each round
+uses eight requests with 65,536 input tokens and one output token, continuously
+replenished by four workers. The three formal samples exclude a warmup round;
+all responses report zero cached tokens.
+
+| Input tokens/s | Replay off | Local-segment tail | Global request tail |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| Sample 1 | 5,658.45 | 9,302.84 | 9,729.21 |
+| Sample 2 | 5,665.05 | 9,301.57 | 9,729.46 |
+| Sample 3 | 5,664.64 | 9,303.91 | 9,729.19 |
+| Median | 5,664.64 | 9,302.84 | 9,729.21 |
+
+The current global-tail version measures **4.58%** above the previous
+local-segment-tail implementation and **71.75%** above replay off. These are
+initial sequential comparisons with three within-arm samples, not independent
+interleaved A/B pairs. Launch arguments match except for
+the off/on replay flag, and all per-round input hashes match. The baseline predates the replay
+patch and a non-executable type annotation in shared Engram; it has not been
+rerun on the final source. The runtime reuses the lab's compiled extensions,
+rather than a clean full build. Backend autotuning was not explicitly frozen
+across engine restarts. No SGLang-relative or decode speedup is claimed.
+
+This follows the existing bounded-replay semantics, including its SWA window
+floor. The canaries do not prove logit equivalence to replay-disabled execution
+or replace a broader model-quality evaluation.
+

+

+# DeepSeek-V4.1 PCP with decode-only CUDA graphs
+
+The NVIDIA MRV2 path supports `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` for DeepSeek-V4.1 PCP.
+Prefill, including decoder SWA bounded replay, remains eager. This builds on
+the PCP baseline, fixed DSpark verification and shared Engram storage, and
+bounded replay from [#59857](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59857),
+[#61553](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61553), and
+[#61554](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61554).
+
+## Metadata and dispatch
+
+Reuse the existing MRV2 target and DFlash/DSpark graph managers. Metadata is
+prepared before graph execution, so tensors referenced by captured kernels
+must retain their storage across requests:
+
+- Copy gathered SWA positions and compressed attention/indexer cache slots
+  into persistent buffers.
+- Update compressor gather indices, retained ring-write slots and predecessor
+  indices in place. Captured dummy inputs must not freeze the ring links used
+  after a rejected draft or a change in PCP request ownership.
+- Match decode graphs using the largest rank-local request count and the
+  existing rank-local token count. Global input staging still reserves space
+  for all requests before PCP partitions them.
+
+The computation, weights, quantization and speculative acceptance policy are
+unchanged. The existing replicated draft and proposal broadcast are reused.
+Generic PCP graph capture from
+[#53867](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53867) is not reimplemented.
+
+## Configuration and limits
+
+Remove `--enforce-eager` and select `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`. For example, the
+H20 validation used this bounded capture ladder:
+
+```bash
+--compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[5,6,10,12,20,24,40,48],"max_cudagraph_capture_size":48}'
+--cudagraph-metrics
+```
+
+Capture sizes must accommodate both target verification and draft queries.
+The example covers the tested DSpark5 target and draft batches through global
+concurrency eight; it is not a universal tuning recommendation. Unmatched
+runtime sizes retain the existing eager fallback. Capture logs alone do not
+prove replay; check the target's runtime `CUDAGraph Stats` as well.
+
+Existing V4.1 PCP restrictions remain: PP=DP=DCP=1, no microbatching, KV
+transfer, prefix caching or MegaMoE, and fixed DSpark verification when
+speculation is enabled. Speculative graphs require the indexer's existing
+flattened or varlen query path. Native speculative query metadata that cannot
+refresh empty decode owners remains rejected. Prefill graph modes are not
+enabled by this change.
+
+## Validation scope
+
+Focused tests cover metadata address stability, request ownership changes,
+rejected-draft ring updates, local dispatch sizing and configuration guards.
+On four H20 GPUs, TP1/PCP4/EP4 with DSpark5, Humming FP8 activations, bounded
+replay and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` passed 32 fixed GSM8K canaries, eight
+long/ragged boundary checks, and 27 natural-EOS requests at concurrency
+1, 3, 4, 5, 8, 5, 1. Target FULL execution and nonzero real speculative
+acceptance were observed. These are targeted regressions, not a full model
+accuracy evaluation or a claim of bitwise logit equivalence.
+
+Graphs consume persistent memory and can add padding work. Keep capture,
+warmup and performance measurements separate, and compare matching eager and
+graph workloads. H20 results do not establish performance on other GPUs.

+# DeepSeek-V4.1 PCP with DSpark
+
+This experimental follow-up to
+[#59857](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59857) enables fixed-verification
+DSpark and optional same-host Engram table sharing. It is based on
+`7908ee8906475842ba0ecd1c09eed6d878718f05`; the parent's MoE prerequisite
+[#60946](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60946) still applies.
+
+The validated configuration is NVIDIA MRV2, FlashMLA sparse attention,
+PP=DP=DCP=1, expert parallelism, eager execution and synchronous scheduling.
+Prefix caching, bounded replay, model CUDA graphs, adaptive verification,
+microbatching, KV transfer and MegaMoE are outside this validation.
+
+## Compressor state and replicated drafting
+
+Without speculation, the PCP compressor publishes each local chunk's last
+row and retains only the newest open ratio-2 row. Rejection can resume before
+that row, so enabling DSpark requires preserving additional ring history.
+
+For speculative batches, each rank publishes up to one ring capacity of its
+chunk tail. Metadata selects unique writes within the newest ring window,
+retaining the rows needed after rejection without conflicting writes to the
+same ring slot. The non-speculative path keeps its one-row publication.
+
+The generic replicated DSpark path from
+[#56107](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56107) restores target
+auxiliary states to global token order before drafting. Replicated draft
+forwards can still differ numerically across PCP ranks: a model trace found
+identical target inputs and samples but different proposed tokens. Broadcast
+the proposal from PCP rank zero so all target shards verify the same tokens.
+When present, proposal logits and adaptive confidence buffers follow the same
+ownership rule; V4.1 adaptive verification remains disabled by its model guard.
+
+This does not implement
+[#54036](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54036)'s sharded draft
+context-KV precomputation. Draft work is still replicated.
+
+## Engram sharding and sharing
+
+Enable the optional storage mode with:
+
+```bash
+--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"pcp_shared_memory":true}'
+```
+
+Engram hash heads retain their existing TP partition. PCP ranks with the same
+TP rank map the same physical weight and scale pages; they do not split the
+table into new PCP-owned row ranges. For example:
+
+| Topology | TP head partitions | Physical copies of each partition |
+| --- | ---: | ---: |
+| TP1 / PCP4, private | 1 | 4 |
+| TP1 / PCP4, shared | 1 | 1 |
+| TP2 / PCP2, private | 2 | 2 |
+| TP2 / PCP2, shared | 2 | 1 |
+
+Each PCP replica still looks up its own token IDs. This reuses the existing
+`DPSharedEngramStorage` allocation, one-writer loading, CUDA host registration,
+UVA views and lifetime handling from
+[#57651](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57651). It does not change
+weight precision, table layout, hash-head ordering or lookup arithmetic.
+Existing DP sharing is unchanged.
+
+The option defaults to false and requires V4.1 CPU offload, PCP>1, DP=PP=1,
+same-host/shared-namespace PCP replicas, and sufficient `/dev/shm` capacity.
+It cannot be combined with `dp_shared_memory` or `use_thp`. Unsupported
+placement or insufficient shared memory raises instead of falling back to
+private copies. The existing storage handles mapping/registration failures.
+
+For the tested checkpoint, two full tables require about 188.83 GiB. Four
+private PCP copies need about 755.33 GiB, exceeding the test container's
+650 GiB limit. Sharing reduced measured table PSS to 188.83 GiB. A 256 GiB
+`/dev/shm` capacity was used within that same 650 GiB container limit; it is
+not an additional host-memory allocation.
+
+Draft models run with PCP=1. Their copied Engram configuration disables PCP
+sharing without modifying the target configuration. This avoids inheriting
+an invalid PCP>1 storage requirement during draft initialization.
+
+This is distinct from
+[#57195](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57195)'s SP token-owner
+lookup path: TP head partitioning and PCP token ownership are preserved here.
+
+## Validation
+
+Four H20 GPUs, real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash checkpoint, DSpark with five speculative
+tokens, chunk size 8192, Humming MoE, `fp8_ds_mla`, APC/replay disabled,
+`--enforce-eager`, `--no-async-scheduling` and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`:
+
+| Check | Result |
+| --- | --- |
+| Distributed Engram suite, including original DP and new TP1/PCP4 and TP2/PCP2 sharing | 31 passed |
+| DSpark configuration suite | 13 passed |
+| Focused PCP compressor GPU regression, PCP2/4 with 0/5/9 speculative tokens | 12 passed |
+| Fixed GSM8K canary, TP1/PCP4 + shared storage | 32/32, no HTTP errors or truncated outputs |
+| Actual speculation counters | 3900 accepted / 5695 drafted, 1139 draft rounds |
+| Shared storage audit | Two backing files, eight rank mappings, total PSS 188.83 GiB |
+
+Storage tests compare private/shared weights, scales and lookup outputs exactly;
+exercise uneven TP head slices, distinct and empty PCP inputs, changed/restored
+CUDA graph inputs, one-writer visibility, failure cleanup and storage lifetime.
+These graph tests validate lookup storage only, not model graph support.
+The model canary is not a comprehensive accuracy evaluation.
+
+Run the focused tests in a CUDA vLLM environment with four free GPUs:
+
+```bash
+python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py
+python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_dspark_utils.py
+python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
+  -k 'v41_pcp_ring_links or v41_pcp_compressor_preserves'
+```
+
+The local validation used a Python overlay on a prebuilt runtime: source base
+`7908ee8` plus this patch, with native extensions and missing runtime files
+reused from an `a982` image. A clean build from the complete PR head remains
+to be validated. Full-model CI requires the large checkpoint and sufficient
+host RAM; the focused tests extend existing Buildkite test files.
+
+## Initial performance evidence
+
+64K input / one output token, concurrency four, eight requests per round with
+continuous replenishment, zero cached tokens; one calibration then three
+measured rounds per instance:
+
+| Configuration | Round 1 | Round 2 | Round 3 | Median input tok/s |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| TP2 / PCP2, private | 5266.766 | 5270.280 | 5273.134 | 5270.280 |
+| TP1 / PCP4, shared | 5658.446 | 5665.052 | 5664.641 | 5664.641 |
+
+The median increased 7.48% in this sequential topology comparison. It is not
+three independent A/B campaigns or an isolated shared-storage speedup:
+TP/PCP and shared-memory capacity changed, and private PCP4 failed at startup.
+The shared mode removes that memory barrier. Calibration samples, excluded
+from the medians, were 5256.846 and 4095.625 tok/s respectively.
+
+SGLang's historical approximately 17.2K tok/s is not a matched backend result.
+Its TP4/attention-CP4/EP2, FP8-activation MoE and decoder bounded replay differ
+from this TP1/PCP4/EP4, Humming A16, no-replay diagnostic configuration. This
+change does not claim to close that gap or improve decode throughput.
